home.title: An Islamic inheritance calculator that shows its work
home.lede: Tell it who the person left behind. It applies the rules of Fara'id, gives each heir their share and cites the verse each share comes from. It's free, and what you enter stays on your device.
home.meta: No account needed. Works offline once loaded.
home.ios.waitlist: Want the iPhone app? Join the waitlist.
home.ledger.title: Pick a sample family
home.ledger.note.residue: The fixed shares are paid first. Sons and daughters split what's left, and each son gets twice what each daughter gets.
home.ledger.note.umariyyatan: The mother gets a third of what's left after the wife's share, not a third of the whole estate. This is the 'Umariyyatan ruling, and the father takes the rest.
home.ledger.note.awl: The fixed shares add up to more than the whole estate, so every share is scaled down by the same proportion. This is called 'awl.
home.ledger.note.radd: The fixed shares add up to less than the whole estate and there's no residuary heir, so the remainder goes back to the heirs in proportion. This is called radd.
home.ledger.open: Open this family in the calculator
home.shares.title: The six shares named in the Quran
home.shares.lede: Surah an-Nisa sets out six fixed fractions. Heirs who don't get one of them, like sons, take whatever is left once the fixed shares are paid.
home.shares.half: The husband, if there are no children. A single daughter with no son. One full sister on her own.
home.shares.quarter: The husband, if there are children. The wife, if there are none.
home.shares.eighth: The wife, if there are children.
home.shares.twoThirds: Two or more daughters with no son. Two or more full sisters.
home.shares.third: The mother, with no children and fewer than two siblings. Two or more maternal siblings, split between them.
home.shares.sixth: The father or mother, if there are children. A single maternal sibling.
home.schools.title: The five schools of thought
home.schools.lede: The schools agree on the fixed shares. They differ on a handful of cases, like a grandfather inheriting alongside brothers. Pick a school before you start, or put all five next to each other for the same family.
home.pro.title: If you handle estates for other people
home.pro.lede: FairShare Pro keeps each family's case in one place, with named heirs, real amounts after debts and bequests, and a PDF on your own letterhead. It's $9 a month or $89 a year.
